steps.title: Put on goggles
steps.instruction: Concentrated sulfuric acid and glacial ethanoic acid are corrosive. Ethanol is highly flammable: no flames today. Goggles on.

whatIf.no_ppe: A single splash in an unprotected eye can cause lasting damage, which is why goggles go on before any bottle is opened.

steps.title: 2 mL ethanol
steps.instruction: Pour 2 mL of ethanol into the boiling tube.

whatIf.no_ppe: Ethanol vapour catches fire from a flame a long way off; the Bunsen must stay off.

steps.title: 2 mL ethanoic acid
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL of glacial ethanoic acid. Pour slowly: it is corrosive and smells strongly of vinegar.

whatIf.too_fast: Glacial ethanoic acid burns skin and its vapour stings the eyes and nose.

steps.title: 3 drops of concentrated sulfuric acid
steps.instruction: Add 3 drops of concentrated sulfuric acid, one at a time. It is the catalyst.

whatIf.wrong_amount: More concentrated acid makes the mixture spit and char; a few drops is enough to catalyse it.
whatIf.too_fast: Concentrated sulfuric acid gets hot as it mixes; adding it fast can make the mixture spit.

steps.title: Into the hot water bath
steps.instruction: Stand the boiling tube in the beaker of hot water from the kettle. Never use a Bunsen with ethanol.

whatIf.wrong_order: Heating with a naked flame instead of a water bath can set the ethanol vapour alight.

steps.title: Let it react
steps.instruction: Leave it in the bath for a few minutes (speed up time) while the ester forms.

steps.title: Waft and smell
steps.instruction: Waft the vapour towards your nose with your hand. Never sniff directly from the tube.

whatIf.no_ppe: Sniffing straight from the tube pulls a strong dose of acid vapour into your nose and lungs.

safe-2.text: Pick up the goggles and put them on before you touch any bottle.

eth-2.text: Pick up the ethanol and pour 2 mL into the boiling tube.

acid-2.text: Pour 2 mL of glacial ethanoic acid into the same tube.

cat-1.text: A catalyst speeds up the reaction.

cat-2.text: Pick up the concentrated sulfuric acid and add drops one at a time to the tube.

bath-2.text: Pick up the boiling tube and choose Into water bath, then the beaker.

bath-3.text: Watch the tube go into the bath.

wait-2.text: Wait or speed up time until a note says the ester has formed.

waft-2.text: Select the tube and choose Waft to smell.

observations.whatHappened: At first the mixture smelled sharply of vinegar. After a few minutes in the hot water bath a sweet, fruity smell like pear drops appeared and a thin oily layer formed.
observations.why: An alcohol (ethanol) and a carboxylic acid (ethanoic acid) react to make an ester (ethyl ethanoate) and water. The reaction is slow and reversible, so a few drops of concentrated sulfuric acid are used as a catalyst and the mixture is warmed. A water bath is used instead of a flame because ethanol is very flammable. Esters have sweet, fruity smells, which is why they are used in perfumes and flavourings.
realWorld: Fats and oils are esters too

prompts.question: What did the product smell like?
prompts.explain: Esters have sweet, fruity smells. Ethyl ethanoate smells like pear drops.

prompts.question: What was the concentrated sulfuric acid for?
choices: It is a reactant that ends up in the ester
prompts.explain: It speeds up the reaction without being used up.

prompts.question: Why warm the tube in a water bath, not over a Bunsen?
prompts.explain: Ethanol vapour catches fire easily, so no naked flames.

safety.title: Naked flame near ethanol
safety.message: You lit a Bunsen with ethanol on the bench. Its vapour can catch fire and flash back to the bottle. Always warm ethanol in a hot water bath.

captions.text: Goggles on. No flames today: ethanol is highly flammable.
...and a carboxylic acid (ethanoic acid): it smells of vinegar.
Three drops of concentrated sulfuric acid: the catalyst.
Warm it in hot water from a kettle, never over a flame.
Alcohol + carboxylic acid → ester + water. The reaction is slow and reversible.
Waft, don't sniff: a sweet, fruity smell. That's ethyl ethanoate, an ester.
